title: Forward and backward stack operational semantics realize the paired Dialectica procedural interpreter
source_version: Official published CSL2026.22 CC BY4.0 HTML/PDF Theorem8 and full author AppendixA, retrieved2026-10-14; same work as fixed CC BY4.0 arxiv2501.16208v2, whose raw third-party-style archive is not an asset

license.name: CC BY4.0 (official published text and diagrams)

difficulty_reason: The author construction couples arbitrary abstract-state commands with a backward counterwitness component: forward evaluation builds synchronized stacks of intermediate states and backward commands, reverse evaluation consumes those stacks to implement the nonlocal Dialectica composition, and a wellfounded descent condition extends this construction to while loops. The complete program/recursive-operator construction and the actual author adequacy proof are retained. The authors call the appendix structural inductions routine, which is preserved; H2 rests on this concrete paired operational construction rather than on claiming the induction is itself difficult or on paper identity.
core_obligations: Retain arbitrary-command and provable while-body descent hypothesis in the exact operational theorem.
Retain both forward existence/result and universally quantified backward stack-extension/result conclusions together as one target.

Retain exact abstract S/T state assumptions, primitive forward/backward commands, defining recursion and all operational rules/while proof; no invented encoding, corrected state type or additional assumption.

standard_prerequisites.name: Higher-order Heyting arithmetic WE-HA omega, SystemT and standard wellfounded induction/finite-sequence representation
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Original Section2 and references18/19 plus exact current abstract-type/while extension. All current backward-while constructors and operational adequacy proof are actually retained.
